scores.evidence: These are prerequisites, and everything after depends on them.
scores.rationale: Phases run decisions → foundations → templates → pilot → CD → migration, with an explicit critical path, though observability is placed later than ideal.

scores.evidence: Phase 3: Pick 2–3 services... Migrate them onto the template and fix the rough edges.
scores.rationale: No thin end-to-end prod path exists in Phase 0; the first real deploy comes in Phase 4 after much foundation work, and Phase 0 is only discovery.

scores.evidence: CD model (GitOps with Argo CD or Flux is my default for this scale)
scores.rationale: Decisions are listed, but only one has a default and none has a flip condition. The 'Where the plan would change' section gives partial conditions.

scores.evidence: Start with low-risk and standard-tier services, and do the critical tier last, once the platform is proven.
scores.rationale: Pipeline templates are called the biggest lever and identity/infra come first, but the migration order puts leaf work first and there is no explicit blast-radius ordering within phases.

scores.evidence: Add security gates in warn-only mode first: SAST, dependency scanning, secret scanning, image scanning, and SBOM generation.
scores.rationale: Security appears in Phases 1, 2 and 5, but Phase 0, Phase 3 and the migration phase have little, and enforcement comes late.

scores.evidence: Pipeline and deployment observability: DORA dashboards, and deploy markers in your monitoring.
scores.rationale: Observability is a late Phase 5 item, even though the plan warns against leaving it until the end. Only DORA metrics are defined early, and Phase 1–3 have no observability.

scores.evidence: Target infrastructure as code: clusters, namespaces, and networking, with Terraform or similar.
scores.rationale: IaC, versioned templates, GitOps and ephemeral runners give reproducibility, but it is not treated explicitly or in every phase.

scores.evidence: Keep the old pipelines running in parallel until each service has had a successful prod deploy on the new one.
scores.rationale: Resilience shows up in Phase 4 (rollback, canary) and Phase 6 (parallel running), but it is missing from the early phases.
The plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, so it does not declare N/A.
Phase 7 lists later work and the audit trails are conditional, but none of it has pull-forward triggers beyond the scenario notes.

note: This is a competent conventional phased plan with sound dependency ordering. It has no walking skeleton, observability and resilience come late, decisions lack flip conditions, and it never addresses the AI question.
